title: operator: add maintenance lock + rolling schema sanitizer to protect private upgrades
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Private deployments have had several near-miss upgrade incidents caused by latent destructive schema changes and uncoordinated operator-driven rolling upgrades. This PR introduces two complementary protections: a cluster-level maintenance lock (operator CRD) to gate automated upgrades and a rolling schema sanitizer preflight that validates migrations in an isolated dry-run before the upgrade proceeds.

What this PR delivers (high level):
- New CRD ClusterUpgradeLock (operator) and an accompanying controller that enforces a cluster-wide maintenance state. When the lock is set, automatic upgrade controllers and CI-driven in-cluster apply agents will bail out with a clear signal. The lock supports an optional expiry TTL and owner annotations for operator-led and manual workflows.
- A "rolling schema sanitizer" job that runs as a Helm pre-upgrade hook and as a standalone Kubernetes Job for Dedicated/Private installer flows. The sanitizer: performs a SQL dry-run against a cloned, short-lived PostgreSQL instance seeded from a logical snapshot (pg_dump/restore), runs migration scripts, checks idempotency, and then runs a lightweight query workload to detect missing indexes and FK regressions.
- Terraform update: installer terraform modules now write an upgrade-manifest blob to the configured object store (S3/GCS) before an upgrade begins. The manifest contains a deterministic SHA256 of the operator image, helm chart checksum, migration set hash, and a human-readable plan. The manifest is used by the sanitizer and by audit tooling.
- Helm chart changes: added pre-upgrade and post-rollback hooks, a new values subtree for maintenanceLock, and a chart-checksum validation in the chartmuseum publish pipeline.
- Safety-first rollout: the operator will hold upgrades when ClusterUpgradeLock is present; the chart’s pre-upgrade hook runs the sanitizer and will fail the release if the sanitizer reports any destructive non-reversible operations or failing idempotency checks.

Why this is different from previous work: earlier PRs added snapshotting, rollback helpers, and gating based on backups. This PR focuses on preventing schema-level regressions by running deterministic dry-runs against cloned data and introducing an operator-level lock for planned maintenance windows (TTL + owner annotations). The approach reduces blast radius for mis-specified migrations and gives SREs a single knob to pause automation across all in-cluster controllers.

Implementation notes:
- ClusterUpgradeLock CRD: apiVersion: installer.redwood.com/v1alpha1 kind: ClusterUpgradeLock spec: {owner, reason, expiryTimestamp}. The controller reconciles and writes a status.conditions to surface the lock state. Controllers that respect the lock consult the API and respect both hard locks and soft advisory locks.
- Sanitizer job: implemented as a small Go binary (cmd/sanitizer) with flags for source snapshot path, migration directory, and a --dry-run-mode that prevents any writes to long-lived resources. Uses lib/pgtmp to spawn ephemeral PG instance in the cluster namespace; timeboxed to 10 minutes by default. Outputs a deterministic JSON report to stdout and to object store.
- Terraform changes: module/upgrade-manifest writes manifest.json to object store and sets a lock key with TTL to avoid concurrent upgrades. The module optionally integrates with Vault for signed manifests.
- Helm: added templates/hooks/sanitizer-preupgrade.yaml and hooks/postrollback-cleanup.yaml. Chart values: maintenanceLock.enabled, maintenanceLock.defaultTTL, sanitizer.image, sanitizer.resources.

Testing and validation:
- Local integration: ran full end-to-end in k3s cluster using synthetic 50MB dataset and a representative migration set (rename, add non-null column with default, index creation). Sanitizer caught a migration that dropped and recreated FK in wrong order; the test ensured the release was blocked.
- CI: unit tests for ClusterUpgradeLock controller (controller-runtime) and sanitizer's migration dry-run harness. Added an integration GH action that runs sanitizer against a lightweight snapshot; flakiness mitigations added (retry on transient DB connection errors).
- Canary: deployed to one internal Private staging cluster for 48 hours; exercised manual lock toggles and TTL expiry.

Rollout and rollback plan:
- Feature flagged via values. Default is off for existing customers. Recommend enabling in a single tenant test, then roll to 10% of customers, then to 100%.
- If sanitizer fails unexpectedly in a target environment, the upgrade can be forced by removing ClusterUpgradeLock or disabling pre-upgrade hooks while capturing sanitizer reports for troubleshooting. Operator supports a soft-warning mode (log-only) that can be used during gradual rollout.

Risks and mitigations:
- False positives: addressed by conservative sanitizer rules and a soft-warning mode.
- Timeouts on large databases: sanitizer is timeboxed and configured with targets; larger clusters should use an out-of-band rehearsal. We added clear error messages to avoid silent failures.
- State drift from snapshot restore: the sanitizer uses logical restore and marks the manifest with the snapshot identifier to ensure repeatability.

Related work items: ENG-8892 (upgrade-safety), ENG-9001 (restore-auditing), and a follow-up ticket ENG-9133 to add signed manifest verification.

Checklist: automated tests added, migration dry-run examples in docs, release notes entry drafted.
release_notes: Add maintenance lock CRD and rolling schema sanitizer preflight. Terraform writes upgrade manifest with checksum. Helm hooks for pre-upgrade sanitizer and post-rollback cleanup. Off by default for existing customers.

review_thread: Arjun Patel (2025-11-06): Great direction. Can you make sure the TTL on the lock is configurable per-namespace for Private installs? Also ask we log the manifest URL in release events.
Maya Chen (2025-11-06): Responded - TTL is cluster-global for now but we added annotations to scope owner and intent. Will follow up with ENG-9133 to add namespace-scoped locks if needed.

Sofia Martinez (2025-11-10): Left a nit on the controller reconciliation loop - suggest backoff jitter to avoid thundering herd when many controllers poll the lock. Also requested clearer error codes from sanitizer.
Maya Chen (2025-11-11): Addressed Sofia's comments - added exponential backoff + jitter and standardized sanitizer exit codes. Updated tests.
Liam O'Connor (2025-11-13): Verified integration in staging. One flaky DB connection in the CI runner - reran and marked pass. Approving after CI green.
SRE Team (2025-11-17): Deployed to internal canary and exercised forced-lock/unlock flows. No regressions observed. Approved for merge.
